14 people have died in ICE custody so far in 2026, already more than all of 2024. But the official count is only part of the story, and what's *not* counted might say even more about the true human costs of detention. A thread on what the numbers hide. 🧵

Too many people seem to simply accept, axiomatically, that migrants' lives are disposable and that some amount of routine detention death is acceptable -- and then work up from there, demanding that the data prove that we should care if mortality exceeds certain bounds. This is anti-humanism.

There is a mini-conversation happening right now about the "per capita" ICE detention death rate. The assumptions built into this are that if ICE expands detention and only a proportional number of people die, then it's okay. Stop playing into that narrative.
